ihram_0: Before you reach the Miqat, the boundary where ihram begins, take a full bath and trim your nails. Men may perfume their body, but not their clothes.
ihram_1: Men wear two white unstitched cloths and sandals. Women wear their usual modest clothes, with the face and hands uncovered.
ihram_2: At the Miqat, make your intention for Umrah. If you are flying, the crew announces the Miqat, so be ready before take-off.
ihram_3: If you fear that illness may stop you, you may add this condition. It is a mercy for older and sick pilgrims.
ihram_4: Now repeat the Talbiyah often until you reach the Kaaba. Men say it aloud, women softly.
ihram_5: While in ihram, avoid perfume, cutting hair or nails, and marital relations. Men do not cover their head.
enter_0: Every gate of the Haram has a number and a name. Note them down or take a photo before you enter. This is your meeting point if you are separated from your group.
enter_1: Enter with your right foot first and say the supplication for entering the mosque.
enter_2: This is the Kaaba. Take your time. Make any supplication you wish, in your own language.
enter_3: Zamzam water is available in coolers all around the mosque. Drink and rest whenever you need. Umrah has no time limit.
enter_4: Make sure you have wudu before Tawaf. Stop saying the Talbiyah when you begin.
start_0: Walk to the corner of the Kaaba with the Black Stone, set in a silver frame. Tawaf starts and ends here.
start_1: Behind you, a green light on the mosque wall marks the starting line. Use it to see where each circuit begins.
start_2: Men uncover the right shoulder for this Tawaf. Face the Black Stone, raise your right hand towards it, and say these words. Do not push to kiss or touch it. Pointing is enough.
start_3: Now walk counter-clockwise, keeping the Kaaba on your left. Men walk briskly in the first three circuits if they are able.
start_4: You will pass the door of the Kaaba, behind a gold-embroidered curtain. There is no fixed supplication for each circuit. Make dua, remember Allah, or recite Quran, in any language.
start_5: Each time you come back to the Black Stone line, one circuit is complete. Tap the counter so you never lose count.
hijr_0: This low, curved wall is the Hijr Ismail. The area inside is part of the Kaaba, so walk around the outside of the wall.
hijr_1: Above it, the golden waterspout carries rainwater from the roof of the Kaaba.
hijr_2: If you are tired, move towards the outer part of the courtyard or to an upper floor. The circuits are longer, but the crowd is lighter.
hijr_3: If you lose your group, do not stop or walk against the crowd. Finish your circuit and go to your meeting gate.
yemeni_0: This is the Yemeni Corner, the last corner before the Black Stone. Touch it with your right hand only if it is easy. If you cannot, simply walk on, without pointing.
yemeni_1: Between the Yemeni Corner and the Black Stone, say this verse.
yemeni_2: The tall clock tower stands behind this side of the mosque. It helps you find your direction from almost anywhere.
yemeni_3: Continue until you complete seven circuits, ending at the Black Stone. Then men cover their right shoulder again.
maqam_0: This golden structure is the Maqam Ibrahim, the station of the Prophet Ibrahim. Go behind it and recite this verse.
maqam_1: Pray two short rak’ahs. It is recommended to recite Al-Kafirun in the first and Al-Ikhlas in the second. If it is crowded, pray anywhere in the mosque.
maqam_2: Then drink Zamzam water and ask Allah for whatever you wish.
maqam_3: Next comes the Sa’i. Follow the signs to the Mas’a and the hill of Safa.
safa_0: This rock is the hill of Safa, where Sa’i begins. As you approach it the first time, recite this.
safa_1: Face the direction of the Kaaba and raise your hands as in supplication. Say Allahu Akbar three times, then these words. Repeat three times, with your own dua in between.
safa_2: Now walk towards Marwah. Keep to the lane going in your direction and follow the signs above you.
safa_3: Sa’i does not require wudu, and you may stop to rest. If walking is difficult, you may use a wheelchair.
green_0: These green lights mark the stretch where Hajar ran in search of water for her son Ismail.
green_1: Men walk quickly between the green lights if they are able. Women walk at their normal pace.
green_2: There is no fixed supplication here. Ask Allah for whatever you need, in your own words.
marwa_0: This is Marwah. Reaching it completes one length. Face the Kaaba and repeat the same remembrance as at Safa, without the verse.
marwa_1: Returning to Safa is length two. Seven lengths in total, Safa to Marwah and back, ending here at Marwah.
marwa_2: Use the counter. Tap once each time you reach a hill.
done_0: Men shave the whole head, which is best, or shorten the hair evenly. Women cut about a fingertip’s length from the end of their hair.
done_1: Your Umrah is complete, and the restrictions of ihram are lifted. May Allah accept it from you.
meaning_niyyah: Meaning: Here I am, O Allah, for Umrah.
meaning_ishtirat: Meaning: O Allah, I will leave ihram wherever You hold me back.
meaning_talbiyah: Meaning: Here I am, O Allah, here I am. Here I am, You have no partner, here I am. All praise, all blessings and all sovereignty belong to You. You have no partner.
meaning_enter: Meaning: In the name of Allah, and peace and blessings be upon the Messenger of Allah. O Allah, open for me the gates of Your mercy.
meaning_bismillah: Meaning: In the name of Allah, Allah is the Greatest.
meaning_rabbana: Meaning: Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire.
meaning_maqam: Meaning: And take the station of Ibrahim as a place of prayer.
meaning_safa_verse: Meaning: Indeed, Safa and Marwah are among the symbols of Allah. I begin with what Allah began with.
meaning_safa_dhikr: Meaning: There is no god but Allah alone, without partner. His is the dominion and the praise, and He has power over all things. There is no god but Allah alone. He fulfilled His promise, gave victory to His servant, and alone defeated the confederates.
